purpose: Additional topic triage pilot using Membrick candidate search, source review, and a stratified audit

topic.definition: DGX Spark DGX OS, OTA, BIOS, firmware, NVIDIA driver, or kernel updates and resulting regressions. A thread is relevant if it supports a reusable, evidence-backed fact, diagnostic procedure, outcome, limitation, or carefully caveated report. Unresolved reports can qualify when their scope and uncertainty are preserved.
topic.exclusions: General hardware/workload problems without an update trigger; recovery-tool requests or recovery design proposals without a concrete update event or regression; unrelated OS changes made for another product or research environment.

searches.query: DGX Spark DGX OS update firmware BIOS driver kernel upgrade regression recovery
DGX Spark apt upgrade NVIDIA driver firmware OTA version mismatch GPU no devices rollback

deduplication.rule: Deduplicate by exact Membrick doc_id before forming candidate pools. Duplicate appearances retain both query ranks in the search result records above.

sampling.method: Three candidates sampled without replacement from each manually triaged pool; IDs sorted lexically before sampling.
sampling.reproducibility_note: The exact algorithm and sorted input pools are recorded here. The sample IDs are retained explicitly below as the audit record.

metrics.definition: Selected is the positive prediction; excluded is the negative prediction. Source review provides the audit label.

calculation.hash_validation_result: All six local source SHA-256 hashes matched the forum exports in the original local corpus.

limitations: The six-document audit is illustrative and does not estimate production performance.
F1 measures classification only inside these retrieved candidate pools; it cannot identify relevant sources missed by both searches.
No false negative appeared in this small sample; this is not evidence that retrieval recall is complete.
The initial candidate pool labels were formed from ranked result content and topic scope; only the sampled six received full source audit.
Membrick source hashes differ from SHA-256 hashes of local raw exports; both values are preserved separately rather than treating them as interchangeable.
